findings.finding: The plan adds step-ID and class fields to every usage-log record written at the runner chokepoint, and batch steps (round_a, round_b) can execute concurrently. The plan specifies no synchronization mechanism (lock, atomic append, queue) for concurrent writes to the shared REBAR_USAGE_LOG file. On Windows and some network filesystems, concurrent appends are not atomic, so two simultaneous records can be interleaved, producing unparseable JSONL lines that break summarize() and defeat the per-step attribution the AC requires.

Linux CI with a network-mounted workspace: O_APPEND atomicity is not guaranteed across NFS/CIFS mounts, same outcome
findings.suggested_fix: Use a per-process or per-thread temp file per concurrent worker and merge/concatenate them into the final REBAR_USAGE_LOG at gate teardown, or guard all writes with a `threading.Lock` if workers are threads rather than processes.

evidence: 'This also outlives the ticket: every future per-pass or per-provider question in this epic (0d76's parity arms, eb6e's cutover, 8625's docs) needs exactly this attribution'
Step 0 has its own ACs (first three AC bullets), own scope (llm/usage_log.py), and own deliverable label ('it is a deliverable in its own right')
The wiring fix has separate ACs (latter AC bullets) touching gate_dispatch.py, runs.py, batch_runner.py
Two different modules, two different reasons to change (observability tooling vs. dispatch wiring)
findings.finding: The plan bundles two independently-releasable outcomes: (1) a general-purpose observability enhancement to `llm/usage_log.py` (step-id and class attribution, explicitly described as valuable to future tickets 0d76, eb6e, 8625 beyond this story) and (2) the actual code-review gate wiring fix. These have different reasons to change (observability/diagnostics tooling vs. bug/wiring fix), touch different modules, and the plan itself says Step 0 'outlives the ticket.' Each could ship, be reviewed, and deliver value independently.
findings.location: Approach / STEP 0 section and 'Then the wiring' section
scenarios: Step 0 delivers a generally useful observability primitive that the rest of the epic depends on — shipping it independently unblocks other work faster
The wiring fix is straightforward once Step 0 provides the diagnostic data — it need not carry the weight of the observability work in the same review/merge cycle
If the wiring fix turns out complex, the observability improvement is held hostage to that complexity
findings.suggested_fix: Split into two tickets: (a) 'Add step-id and class attribution to REBAR_USAGE_LOG records' (scope: llm/usage_log.py, ACs = current first three bullet points); (b) 'Wire model classes through code-review gate' (scope: gate_dispatch.py, runs.py, batch_runner.py, ACs = current remaining bullet points, depends on (a) for diagnostic run).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the exact JSON key names, types, and presence/absence rules for the two new REBAR_USAGE_LOG fields (e.g. `step_id: str | null` and `model_class: str | null`) in the plan, co-located with the AC that asserts them, so writer (record()), reader (summarize()), and tests all use the same vocabulary.
evidence: AC bullet 1: 'every REBAR_USAGE_LOG record carries the STEP ID of the step that made the call, in addition to the existing op (prompt name). Asserted by a test that runs a gate with the log enabled and checks the recorded step ids'
AC bullet 2: 'a record whose model came from a CLASS token also carries that class'
Existing record() signature: `def record(usage: dict, *, op: str, model: str | None = None, provider: str | None = None)` — new parameters must be named
summarize() at usage_log.py:227 accesses row fields by key (`row.get('op', '?')`, `row.get('model')`) — new fields need defined key names to remain inert/additive
The AC test 'checks the recorded step ids' must reference a specific key name — undefined in the plan
ABSENCE: no key name like 'step', 'step_id', 'step_name', or 'model_class', 'class', 'resolved_class' appears anywhere in the plan text
findings.finding: The two new REBAR_USAGE_LOG JSONL fields ('step id of the step that made the call' and 'that class, so a reader can tell resolved to opus because frontier from resolved to opus because cfg.model') are referenced throughout ACs and described as inputs to test assertions and summarize() compatibility checks, but neither field's JSON key name, type, nor presence/absence rule is defined anywhere in the plan.
findings.location: AC bullets 1 and 2; Step 0 section ('record the STEP ID (and the resolved model's declared CLASS, when the value came from a class token) alongside op on every usage record'); usage_log.py:114 record() signature
scenarios: Implementer chooses key name 'step' for step-id; test author uses 'step_id'; assertions fail silently or require a second negotiation
summarize() gains a new branch that reads the new key but the CI summary script parses a different key name — the additive-safety AC passes in unit tests but breaks in CI
Downstream epic 0d76 reads 'model_class' but the field is written as 'class' — the per-PASS claim the epic relies on is silently unfalsifiable, exactly the problem the plan was designed to fix
findings.suggested_fix: Add a 'New record schema' sub-section to Step 0 specifying: `step_id` (string, the ctx.step_id value, always present when called from a workflow step, omitted/null otherwise) and `model_class` (string, one of 'trivial'/'standard'/'frontier', present only when resolve_model_string() resolved a class token, omitted otherwise). Name the new record() keyword parameters to match.

findings.finding: AC 4 ('the live probe is RE-RUN after Step 0 and the resulting per-step attribution is recorded in a comment') describes an inherently external artifact — a live LLM run whose output is pasted into a ticket comment — but does NOT carry the [operator-attested] tag. Without the tag the operator-attested rule does not apply, leaving this criterion with no in-repo proving command and no CI-verifiable evidence; an agent cannot determine completion from repo artifacts alone.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — fourth bullet ('the live probe is RE-RUN after Step 0...')
findings.suggested_fix: Prefix the fourth AC bullet with `[operator-attested]`: `- [ ] [operator-attested] the live probe is RE-RUN after Step 0 and the resulting per-step attribution is recorded in a comment — this is what names the broken seam, and it replaces inference with data.`
